pillar_reactions.evidence: Understood it precisely and summarised it back unprompted, which is the clearest comprehension signal in the batch: 'Yeah, that's something I can see myself doing. I'm hearing form is the most important thing with a lighter weight. Three times 20 minutes, I'm going to say 20 minutes per week initially, and then daily mobility five to ten minutes. I think those are the three main takeaways.' No questions and no pushback. Worth noting that his earlier and unresolved fear — that the clean would keep striking his forearm — sat underneath this acceptance and resurfaced later at the commitment check.

Agreed readily — 'yeah sure' — and asked only for the third component to be repeated: 'so the when, the what, and what was the other one'. He had already pre-qualified himself on this pillar by raising his protein struggle as a vegetarian at 85 kg. The exchange is notable for what neither party said: the rep built the nutrition case on fasting and eating windows for a diabetic prospect who fasts every morning under sensor monitoring, and the diabetes was not referenced once during the pillar.

Asked a substantive mechanical question about delivery — 'With the weekly check-ins, are they kind of timetable, or do we just book it week to week?' — and received a clear answer that check-ins are form-based rather than calls. He then made the request that mattered most to him: 'Do you have anyone in the UK that I can speak to who's currently on the program?', clarifying when pressed that he wanted 'someone who is independent and who has their own experience of communication, the support, the accountability' rather than results. This is the pillar he was actively trying to verify and could not.

anchors.raw: I'm comparing it to how many PT sessions or someone local that I might get for the same money, essentially. Even if they charge, I don't know, £50 an hour, £70 an hour, whatever, that's still 10, 7, 8, 9, 10 hours a week, a month, excuse me. So a couple of hours a week for himself.
anchors.competitor: Local UK personal trainers at £50-70 per hour
anchors.note: The decisive anchor. He did the arithmetic live and concluded the same money buys roughly two in-person hours a week for a year — with hands-on form correction, which is precisely what he had just said he needed given five injury sites. It is the same shape as the loss on the Spanish call the same day: an in-person alternative at price parity that better matches a prospect whose primary problem is physical and specific.

anchors.raw: If, for me, that will probably pay for 10 years worth of annual membership where I go at the gym and swim.
anchors.competitor: His existing gym and swimming membership
anchors.note: A ten-to-one framing against his current spend, and materially reinforced by the fact that his current low-cost regime demonstrably works on the goal he cares most about: he had already told the rep that two swims and an hour of yoga a week do 'absolute magic' for his blood sugar. That is a functioning cheap alternative producing measurable results, and the offer never addressed why it needed replacing.

anchors.raw: The one option is kind of, you know, various options, which is just a self-directed, self-directed training, as I've always done with the gym, speaking with colleagues and other, you know, experienced trainers.
anchors.competitor: Himself, plus informal advice from colleagues and experienced trainers
anchors.note: Raised before price was mentioned, which made it a genuine competing option rather than a post-hoc justification. The rep countered reasonably by asking whether self-direction would deliver the accountability the prospect had asked for, and by pointing out that form errors made alone are how injuries happen. The prospect conceded the form point fully — 'you want to be working with someone who can correct your form at that very early stage, undoubtedly' — which arguably strengthened the case for in-person coaching rather than for this offer.

unmet_demand.want: To speak with an independent, current UK client about their experience of the coaching, support and communication
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep had no reference available and said so plainly — 'I've got no idea, to be honest. No idea.' He offered public testimonials and his own experience as a former client now employed by the business, and the prospect explicitly restated that he wanted someone independent. There appears to be no reference process or client list a rep can draw on.

unmet_demand.want: Confidence that the core kettlebell movements will not aggravate five existing injury sites, having felt pain on the clean during a deliberate trial
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Answered only as a form and mobility issue that resolves with practice. No assessment, no movement modification, no physiotherapy input and no clinician clearance were offered or suggested, and the programme contains no mechanism for any of them. The prospect's willingness to commit remained explicitly conditional on this and it was never resolved.

unmet_demand.want: Nutrition and fasting guidance that accounts for diabetes and sensor-monitored blood glucose
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Not addressed. The nutrition pillar was built on intermittent fasting and eating windows, and the rep additionally raised a 24-hour community fast, without any reference to the prospect's diabetes, his medication, or the weak energy levels he had reported minutes earlier. Whether the protocol is safe or appropriate for him is unknown to both parties.

unmet_demand.want: A defined payment structure, asked for directly — 'effectively you pay up front, are you paying monthly?'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep described instalments as existing but unstructured: 'we do sometimes have monthly payments that we split it up over a few months. That's just nothing that we have set in place.' The prospect was given no concrete alternative to a single upfront payment to evaluate.
